audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Gwen Levels 2-3 and 2+ items, while the prose says 'Warwick out-sustains you levels 1-3', 'Levels 4-5 are his window' and 'This stays a true coinflip into the late game'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Warwick/Skill/Skill/Warwick/Gwen/Gwen/Skill and matches the prose.
audit.corrected: Chart realigned in both layers; difficulty 6/10 lowered to 5/10 on a 50.15% win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase rows were template text and none of Warwick's abilities were named anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Packet flags 'never names any of Warwick's abilities'. His windows are Blood Hunt coming online and Infinite Duress; Gwen's are Level 6 Mist and Riftmaker plus Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast, Blood Hunt, Primal Howl and Infinite Duress named with cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Infinite Duress a 'point-blank single-target suppress' he cannot 'target' from outside the mist, and never states the health thresholds that gate his whole kit.
audit.why: Riot on Infinite Duress: 'Warwick leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed), suppressing the first champion he collides with' — it is a directional leap onto a collision, not a targeted point-blank cast, and its distance grows with his bonus move speed. Riot on Blood Hunt: 'Warwick senses enemies below 50% health, gaining Move Speed toward and attack speed against them. When they fall below 25% health, he frenzies and these bonuses triple' — so staying above 50% denies the chase AND shortens the R leap. Riot on Eternal Hunger: he heals only below 50% health, tripled below 25%. Riot on Primal Howl: 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee' — bursting into it is wasted damage followed by a fear.
audit.corrected: R described as a dodgeable directional leap, the 50%/25% thresholds written in as the thing to play around, and Primal Howl's damage-reduction window added.

audit.whatIsWrong: No numbers, and Infinite Duress was the only tracked cooldown.
audit.why: Blood Hunt 80/70/60/50/40s, Jaws of the Beast 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Primal Howl 15/14/13/12/11s, Infinite Duress 110/90/70s.
audit.corrected: All written into the cooldown block, phase whys and trading rules.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Warwick must walk into your engage range.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Infinite Duress's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Warwick carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.

edits.before: - Warwick Infinite Duress: matchup-defining — His all-in lock. Mist it as he commits. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Warwick Blood Hunt (40-80s): it only tracks enemies under 50% health, so staying topped up removes his speed and R range. - Jaws of the Beast (6-8s): max-health damage that heals him. - Primal Howl (11-15s): 2.5s damage cut, then a fear.

edits.before: Good trade: Stack passive on minions, E onto Warwick with the center-Q ready, snip the %HP true damage, and W if he turns. edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his window — Q heal plus W move speed lets him run you down with no Hallowed Mist yet to break it, so hold near your tower and don't get walked into. Everything flips at 6, but play it right: his R is a point-blank single-target suppress, and untargetability won't cancel a lock that already landed. Pre-drop your mist BEFORE he commits so he can't even target the R from outside the fog — then snip him while he's stuck whiffing his all-in. From there you trade evenly because your healing-on-damage answers his healing-on-drain.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his window — Q heal plus Blood Hunt move speed runs you down with no Hallowed Mist yet to break it, so hold near tower. Everything flips at 6, but play it right: Infinite Duress is a directional leap that suppresses the first champion it collides with, and its distance scales with his bonus move speed, so staying above 50% health keeps Blood Hunt off you and the leap short. Pre-drop mist before he commits and sidestep the line — then snip him while he whiffs. From there you trade evenly, because your healing-on-damage answers his healing-on-drain.

notes: Infinite Duress was described as a point-blank targeted suppress; Riot's text makes it a directional leap onto the first champion it collides with, whose distance scales with his bonus move speed. That reframes the counterplay from 'be untargetable' to 'stay above 50% health so Blood Hunt never marks you, then sidestep the line'. The 50%/25% thresholds gate his passive, his W and his R range and appeared nowhere on the page.
